verses.zh: 第六年六月初五日，我坐在家中；犹大的众长老坐在我面前。在那里主耶和华的灵（原文是手）降在我身上。
verses.en: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month,[NOTE:1] as I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting in front of me, the hand[NOTE:2] of the Sovereign Lord seized me.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX reads “In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month.” sn In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month would be September 17, 592 b.c., about fourteen months after the initial vision.

Hand in the OT can refer metaphorically to power, authority, or influence. In Ezekiel God’s hand being on the prophet is regularly associated with communication or a vision from God (3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1).tn Or “power.”
Heb “fell upon me there,” that is, God’s influence came over him.
verses.commentary:
8:1 "It came about in the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month" This day relates to the
exile of the Davidic seed (Jehoiachin) from Jerusalem to Babylon (cf. Ezek. 1:2). Ezekiel uses this dating reference
throughout his book (cf. Ezek. 1:2; 8:1; 20:1; 24:1; 26:1; 29:1,17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1,17; 33:21; 40:1). This same
dating reference is also seen in 2 Kgs. 25:27; Jer. 52:31.

▣ "with the elders of Judah sitting before him" This shows that the symbolic physical positions of
Ezek. 4:4-8 did not last all day and all night.

The "elders" were local tribal or clan leaders. This meant they were the civil leadership of towns,
villages, and communities. They dealt with individual Israelites on a local level. Here they are the tribal
leaders from Judea who have been exiled by Nebuchadnezzar II to an exilic community by the canal Chebar. The fact
that the elders would come and consult with Ezekiel shows his reputation (i.e. "sitting before me"). What a contrast
between the elders of Judah, who would seek God's counsel from Ezekiel, and the elders of the House of Israel,
who are committing idolatry in the temple and at home in Ezek. 8:7-13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER, I. B.

▣ "the hand of the Lord God fell on me there" Notice the anthropomorphic
language. Apparently YHWH's revelations came at different times and at different places. The exact nature
and mechanism of divine inspiration is uncertain, but the reality is certain (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:14,22; 33:22; 37:1;
1 Kgs. 18:46; 2 Kgs. 3:15; Isa. 8:11; Jer. 15:17; 2 Tim. 3:14-16). God has revealed Himself and His will to certain human instruments
and through them to generations of believers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

verses.zh: 我观看，见有形像彷佛火的形状，从他腰以下的形状有火，从他腰以上有光辉的形状，彷佛光耀的精金。
verses.en: As I watched, I noticed[NOTE:1] a form that appeared to be a man.[NOTE:2] From his waist downward was something like fire,[NOTE:3] and from his waist upward something like a brightness,[NOTE:4] like an amber glow.[NOTE:5]
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb (so also throughout the chapter).
The MT reads “fire” rather than “man,” the reading of the LXX. The nouns are very similar in Hebrew.

The MT reads: “what appeared to be his waist and downwards was fire.” The LXX omits “what appeared to be,” reading: “from his waist to below was fire.” Suggesting that “like what appeared to be” belongs before “fire,” D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:277) points out the resulting poetic symmetry of form with the next line, as followed in the translation here.
The LXX omits “like a brightness.”
See Ezek 1:4.
verses.commentary:
8:2 Although this appearance (BDB 909) is very similar to the description of anthropomorphic deity in
Ezek. 1:26, 27, this verse seems to describe angelic agency (typical of apocalyptic literature; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE).

The MT has "a form that had the appearance of fire." The term "fire" (BDB 77) is repeated later in
the verse. The Septuagint translates a similar Hebrew word "man" (BDB 35). The UBS Text Project, p. 21,
suggests that the MT had "fire" but that the LXX is a more ancient form.

- man ‒ איש

- fire ‒ אש

▣ "fire" See note at Ezek. 1:27 and SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ "brightness, like the appearance of glowing metal" See note at Ezek. 1:4,27.

verses.zh: 他伸出彷佛一只手的样式，抓住我的一绺头发，灵就将我举到天地中间，在　神的异象中，带我到耶路撒冷朝北的内院门口，在那里有触动主怒偶像的坐位，就是惹动忌邪的。
verses.en: He stretched out the form[NOTE:1] of a hand and grabbed me by a lock of hair on my head. Then a wind[NOTE:2] lifted me up between the earth and sky and brought me to Jerusalem[NOTE:3] by divine visions, to the door of the inner gate that faces north where the statue[NOTE:4] that provokes to jealousy was located.
notes: The Hebrew term is normally used as an architectural term in describing the pattern of the tabernacle or temple or a representation of it (see Exod 25:8; 1 Chr 28:11).
Or “spirit.” See note on “wind” in 2:2.
For the location of Jerusalem see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Or “image.”
verses.commentary:
8:3 "He. . .the Spirit" The angelic being is parallel or equated with "a spirit" (no ARTICLE in Hebrew text, cf. Ezek. 3:12; 11:1). Often
the Spirit (BDB 924) represents YHWH's presence, in this case an angelic being, transports the prophet (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:12; 2 Kgs. 2:16;
Ezek. 3:12,14; 8:3; 11:24; 37:1; possibly Acts 8:26-27,39). See notes at Ezek. 2:2

I do not think that there are two spiritual beings involved in this transport of the prophet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "lifted" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724) is used in

- v. 3 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Ezekiel is lifted,
cf. Ezek. 3:12,14; 11:1,24; 43:5

- v. 5 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, Ezekiel is commanded to lift
his eyes

- v. 5 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, he lifts his eyes

▣ "in the visions of God" "Visions" (BDB 909) is a means of receiving divine revelation (cf. Gen. 46:2;
Num. 12:6; 1 Sam. 3:15; Dan. 10:16; Ezek. 1:1; 8:3; 40:2). Whether this involved

- sight (cf. Ezek. 8:2,4,5,6,7,10,11)

- hearing (cf. Ezek. 8:5,6,8,9,12)

- mental images (cf. Ezek. 8:3,4,7)

is not always clear. See note at the beginning of the chapter, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "to the entrance to the north gate of the inner court" This gate is called the
Altar Gate in Ezek. 8:4. We learn from Lev. 1:11 that this was the place of sacrifice. It was known as the
royal entrance because it faced the palace of the king.

▣ "the idol of jealousy" There has been much discussion as to the exact nature of this idol or
image (BDB 702). Idolatry caused a powerful reaction from YHWH (cf. Exod. 20:3-4)! Jealousy (BDB 888) is a
word of deep passion. It is obvious that the idol had a prominent place at the entrance to the temple of
YHWH (cf. Ezek. 8:3,5; Jer. 7:30; 32:34).

- Some have supposed that because of 2 Kings 21:3,7; 23:6 that it was the carved image of Ashtoreth, the Canaanite
female fertility goddess. If so, this reflected Canaanite idolatry.

- Others supposed it was a statue of a temple guardian (i.e. lion, sphinx), if so, then Babylonian idolatry.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL

verses.zh: 谁知，在那里有以色列　神的荣耀，形状与我在平原所见的一样。
verses.en: Then I perceived that the glory of the God of Israel was there, as in the vision I had seen earlier in the valley.
verses.commentary:
8:4 The portable throne chariot of God that Ezekiel saw in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 1:26-28) was also present
in the temple.

verses.zh: 神对我说：「人子啊，你举目向北观看。」我就举目向北观看，见祭坛门的北边，在门口有这惹忌邪的偶像；
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, look up toward[NOTE:1] the north.” So I looked up toward the north, and I noticed to the north of the altar gate was this statue of jealousy at the entrance.
notes: Heb “lift your eyes (to) the way of.”
verses.commentary:
8:5 "He said to me. . ." Who is speaking? There are several subjects involved in this context.

- the Lord God fell on Ezekiel, v. 1

- the spiritual being described in v. 2 and lifted Ezekiel up, v. 2

- a spirit is also involved in the transportation of Ezekiel to the temple, v. 3

- the glory of the God of Israel was in the temple, v. 4; 9:3 (related to Ezekiel 1); also mentioned in 9:3

- the "He" of v. 5 identifies Himself as the owner of the temple (i.e. YHWH) in v. 5. This same representation of
Deity speaks and leads Ezekiel in 8:7-13,14-15,16-18, and continues in chapter 9

- personsified executioners are summoned in 9:1,5,7

- "a certain man clother in linen" in 9:2,4,11

▣ "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

NASB
"that I would be far from My sanctuary"

NKJV
"to make Me go far away from My sanctuary"

NRSV, JPSOA
"to drive Me far from My sanctuary"

TEV
"drawing me farther and farther away from my

holy place"

NJB
"to drive Me out of my sanctuary"

The VERBAL (BDB 934, KB 1221, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) expresses the reason for YHWH's departure
(cf. Ezek. 11:22-23) from the temple, which He promised never to leave (cf. 2 Sam. 7:13,16, but
Jeremiah saw this event, cf. Jer. 33:17,21). The Mosaic Covenant was unconditional on God's part but conditional
on Israel's part (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CONVENANT).

Both the LXX and Peshitta translate this phrase in such a way as to refer to Israel
being addressed. The MT supports that it is YHWH who is driven away.

verses.zh: 又对我说：「人子啊，以色列家所行的，就是在此行这大可憎的事，使我远离我的圣所，你看见了吗？你还要看见另有大可憎的事。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the people[NOTE:1] of Israel are practicing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? But you will see greater abominations than these!”
notes: Heb “house.”
verses.commentary: 8:6 "the great abomination" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

verses.zh: 他领我到院门口。我观看，见墙上有个窟窿。
verses.en: He brought me to the entrance of the court, and as I watched, I noticed a hole in the wall.
verses.commentary:
8:7 "the entrance of the court" This refers to the outer court of Solomon's temple.

▣ "a hole in the wall" This implies that this particular idolatry was done in secret by the leaders of
the people.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，你要挖墙。」我一挖墙，见有一门。
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, dig into the wall.” So I dug into the wall and discovered a doorway.
verses.commentary:
8:8 "now dig through the wall" This VERB (BDB 369, KB 365) is used twice.

- Qal IMPERATIVE

- Qal IMPERFECT with waw

It is uncertain how "the hole" of Ezek. 8:7 is related to the new hole of Ezek. 8:8, dug
by Ezekiel. The first may have been a secret entrance for the idolaters (cf. Ezek. 8:11-12) and the
second an access hole for Ezekiel to view the abominations occurring there (cf. Ezek. 8:10-13).

verses.zh: 他说：「你进去，看他们在这里所行可憎的恶事。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Go in and see the evil abominations they are practicing here.”
verses.commentary:
8:9 "Go in and see" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES.

- BDB 97, KB 112, cf. Ezek. 8:10

- BDB 906, KB 1157, cf. Ezek. 8:11

verses.zh: 我进去一看，谁知，在四面墙上画着各样爬物和可憎的走兽，并以色列家一切的偶像。
verses.en: So I went in and looked. I noticed every figure[NOTE:1] of creeping thing and beast—detestable images[NOTE:2]—and every idol of the house of Israel, engraved on the wall all around.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “pattern.”
Heb “detestable.” The word is often used to describe the figures of foreign gods.
These engravings were prohibited in the Mosaic law (Deut 4:16-18).
verses.commentary:
8:10 "every form of creeping things and beasts and detestable things" This may relate to the
worship of animals as reflected in Egyptian idolatry (cf. Exodus 32, a golden calf, later copied at the
temples in Bethel and Dan). For Israel, they were to make no image of these unclean (cf. Leviticus 11;
Deuteronomy 14) animals (cf. Deut. 4:18). These prohibitions were to isolate Israel from Canaanite worship.
Much of the Levitical legislation is for this purpose.

▣ "were carved on the wall all around" The VERB (BDB 348, KB 347,
Pual PARTICIPLE) means "to carve" (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:35 or "scratch" cf.
Ezek. 4:1). In Ezek. 23:14 it may refer to wall painting.

verses.zh: 在这些像前有以色列家的七十个长老站立，沙番的儿子雅撒尼亚也站在其中。各人手拿香炉，烟云的香气上腾。
verses.en: Seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel[NOTE:1] (with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them) were standing in front of them, each with a censer in his hand, and fragrant vapors[NOTE:2] from a cloud of incense were swirling upward.
notes: Note the contrast between these seventy men who represented Israel and the seventy elders who ate the covenant meal before God, inaugurating the covenant relationship (Exod 24:1, 9).
The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.
verses.commentary:
8:11 "seventy elders of the house of Israel" "The house of Israel" parallels "the house of Judah."
It also shows the number 70 (cf. Exod. 24:1; Num. 11:16,25) of the elders (cf. Ezek. 7:26) involved in this
idolatry. This would symbolize all of Israel's leadership. Seventy is a round number denoting fullness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

▣ "Jaazaniah the son of Shapan" This shows the radical influence of idolatry when one of the
well known leaders was involved in it (cf. Ezek. 11:1). Shapan is a name related to the court leaders of
Josiah (cf. 2 Kings 22; 2 Chr. 34; Jeremiah 36), but the connection is uncertain. Possibly his name is
meant to convey that the political leadership at the highest levels was involved.

8:11 "each man with his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense rising" They were
all personally involved in the idolatrous rituals.

NASB, NRSV
"fragrance of the cloud of incense rising"

NKJV
"a thick cloud of incense went up"

TEV
"smoke was rising from the incense"

NJB, REB
"rose a fragrant cloud of incense"

Peshitta
"the smoke of the cloud of incense went up"

LXX
"the vapor of the incense was ascending"

The Hebrew term "fragrance" (BDB 801 II) is found only here in the OT. The same consonants mean

- pray

- worshiper

- abundant

- a place name in Josh. 15:42. BDB suggests "odor" (NET), but also possibly "smoke"
(which is a symbol of prayer rising to God)

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，以色列家的长老暗中在各人画像屋里所行的，你看见了吗？他们常说：『耶和华看不见我们；耶和华已经离弃这地。』」
verses.en: He said to me, “Do you see, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in the chamber of his idolatrous images?[NOTE:1] For they think, ‘The Lord does not see us! The Lord has abandoned the land!’”
notes: Heb “the room of his images.” The adjective “idolatrous” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.sn This type of image is explicitly prohibited in the Mosaic law (Lev 26:1).
verses.commentary:
8:12 "each man in a room with its carved images" Not only were these leaders participating in cultic
idolatry in the temple, but they had made local or individual shrines in their own homes (or alcoves of the
temple). It is uncertain if this represents corporate worship or individual worship or both.

▣ "they say" There is a series of excuses and words found in the book of Ezekiel
(cf. Ezek. 8:12; 9:9; 11:3, 15; 12:22, 27; 18:2,25; 33:10, 24, 30; 35:12; 37:11). This is similar to
Paul's use of diatribe in Romans.

▣ "'The Lord does not see us; the Lord
has forsaken the land'" These comments cast aspersions on YHWH's knowledge and His covenant promises!
They were repudiating the character of YHWH (cf. Gen. 3:1-7)! These men had reacted theologically to the
deportations of artisans and leaders from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II in 596 B.C.

verses.zh: 他又说：「你还要看见他们另外行大可憎的事。」
verses.en: He said to me, “You will see them practicing even greater abominations!”
verses.commentary:
8:13 "yet you will see still greater abominations which they are committing" This becomes a repeated
refrain (cf. Ezek. 8:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

verses.zh: 他领我到耶和华殿外院朝北的门口。谁知，在那里有妇女坐着，为搭模斯哭泣。
verses.en: Then he brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the Lord’s house. I noticed[NOTE:1] women sitting there weeping for Tammuz.[NOTE:2]
notes: Given the context, this could be understood as a shock, e.g., idiomatically “Good grief! I saw….”

The worship of Tammuz included the observation of the annual death and descent into the netherworld of the god Dumuzi. The practice was observed by women in the ancient Near East over a period of centuries.
verses.commentary:
8:14 "women were sitting there weeping for Tammuz" See a good, brief article in James M. Freeman,
Manners and Customs of the Bible, pp. 299-300. This reflects the Babylonian idolatry of the Sumerian
agricultural god who died and rose every year. Obviously he became the fertility god of the Babylonians.
He is known in Babylon as Dumuzi, Consort of Ishtar (cf. Isa. 17:10,11). He is known in Greece as
Adonis, which is very similar to the Egyptian Osiris. This was the male lover of Aphrodite who was
killed by wild boars and sent to the underworld each year for six months. The women wept to identify with
Aphrodite, who wept at the loss of her lover during the winter. August to September (cf. Ezek. 8:1) would
have started this cycle. Possibly the worship of Babylonian gods shows that it had already conquered Israel
spiritually!

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，你看见了吗？你还要看见比这更可憎的事。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Do you see this, son of man? You will see even greater abominations than these!”

verses.zh: 他又领我到耶和华殿的内院。谁知，在耶和华的殿门口、廊子和祭坛中间，约有二十五个人背向耶和华的殿，面向东方拜日头。
verses.en: Then he brought me to the inner court of the Lord’s house. Right there[NOTE:1] at the entrance to the Lord’s temple, between the porch and the altar,[NOTE:2] were about 25[NOTE:3] men with their backs to the Lord’s temple,[NOTE:4] facing east—they were worshiping the sun[NOTE:5] toward the east!
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something.
The priests prayed to God between the porch and the altar on fast days (Joel 2:17). This is the location where Zechariah was murdered (Matt 23:35).
The LXX reads “twenty” instead of “twenty-five,” perhaps because of the association of the number twenty with the Mesopotamian sun god Shamash. tn Or “exactly twenty-five.”
The temple faced east.
Or “the sun god.” sn The worship of astral entities may have begun during the reign of Manasseh (2 Kgs 21:5).
verses.commentary:
8:16 "the inner court" This is described in 1 Kgs. 6:36. It was also known as "the Court of the Priests" in
2 Chr. 4:9. It would be the court just before the inner shrine (i.e. holy place and holy of holies).

▣ "twenty-five men" There may be some purposeful symbolism related to the identity of these different
groups.

- The 70 elders and the son of Shapan seem to represent the civil leadership.

- The women seem to represent the general public.

- The twenty-five men may represent priests (i.e. the High Priest and the priests from David's day; the LXX has "twenty").

If so, then all segments of Israeli society were actively involved in idolatry at the temple
(the place YHWH symbolically dwelt).

▣ "with their backs to the temple of the Lord and their faces to the
east. . .toward the sun" The last mentioned Canaanite idolatry was the worship of the sun (i.e.
Deut. 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs. 23:5,11; Jer. 8:2). The worship of the sun is also illustrated by the names of cities:

- Beth Shemesh" ["house of the sun," cf. Josh. 15:10; 21:16; Jdg. 1:33]

- En-shemesh" ["fountain of the sun," cf. Josh. 15:7; 18:17]

- Mount Heres" ["mount of the sun," cf. Jdg. 1:35])

It is ironic symbolism that as they faced the sun they turned their back on the Lord. This sun
worship was rampant all over the Ancient Near East, but particularly in Egypt, Canaan, Babylon, and later in
Persia (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:11). It is also related to the later winged sun disk of Zoroastrianism.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，你看见了吗？犹大家在此行这可憎的事还算为小吗？他们在这地遍行强暴，再三惹我发怒，他们手拿枝条举向鼻前。
verses.en: He said to me, “Do you see, son of man? Is it a trivial thing that the house of Judah commits these abominations they are practicing here? For they have filled the land with violence and provoked me to anger still further. Look, they are putting the branch to their nose![NOTE:1]
notes: It is not clear what the practice of “holding a branch to the nose” indicates. A possible parallel is the Syrian relief of a king holding a flower to his nose as he worships the stars (ANEP 281). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:145-46. The LXX glosses the expression as “Behold, they are like mockers.”
verses.commentary:
8:17 "provoked Me repeatedly" The VERB (BDB 494, KB 491,
Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is regularly used of provoking YHWH to
anger by committing idolatry (cf. Deut. 4:25; 9:18; 31:29; 32:16; 1 Kgs. 14:9,15; 16:7,33; 22:54; 2 Kgs. 17:11,17;
21:6; 23:19; Jer. 25:6,7; 32:30; 44:8; Ezek. 16:25).

▣ "for behold they are putting the twig to their nose" There have been several theories concerning
this phrase:

- we have found this (i.e. a flowered stem held to the nose) as an act of sun worship in Assyrian
bas reliefs (ANEP 281, which fits this context best)

- the early rabbis and later Kimchi and Rashi say it relates to God's nose and thus the stench of idolatry
that rose to Him (JPSOA footnote "c" states "their" is a euphemism for "My")

- it is a sign of contempt and mockery of God (i.e. LXX, Strabo [historian], cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 1118)

verses.zh: 因此，我也要以忿怒行事，我眼必不顾惜，也不可怜他们；他们虽向我耳中大声呼求，我还是不听。」
verses.en: Therefore I will act with fury! My eye will not pity them nor will I spare[NOTE:1] them. When they have shouted in my ears, I will not listen to them.”
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.
verses.commentary: 8:18 See full exegetical note at Ezek. 7:4. Also note this is repeated in 9:10.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the
Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO CHAPTERS 8-11

- Ezekiel chapters 8-11 are one literary unit (cf. Ezek. 8:1 and 11:24).

- This section occurs fourteen months after Ezekiel's original vision of YHWH by the River Chebar; compare Ezek. 1:1-3 with 8:1
(August-September 592 B.C.).

- This is a literary unit which encompasses a vision of the abominations that were occurring in the temple in Jerusalem.
Commentators have been divided on whether this was

- simply a vision ("brought me in the visions of God," Ezek. 8:3; also especially Ezek. 11:24)

- that he was physically transported to Jerusalem ("lifted me up between earth and heaven," Ezek. 8:3)

The details of both the temple and the people involved are very specific.

- Much of this flagrant idolatry can be attributed to the influence of King Manasseh (cf. 2 Kings 21), also notice
King Josiah's reform in 2 Kings 23.
